findings.evidence: Exp.lean:111 `@[expose]`, :133 `:= rfl`; Exponential.lean:102 `rw [coe_expSMulHom]`. The repo's sealing convention `:= (rfl)` is used 400 times across 127 files, e.g. `Associative.lean:66 dividedPower_def ... := (rfl)`.
findings.fix: Drop `@[expose]` and prove `coe_expSMulHom := (rfl)`; the `rfl` still elaborates in the defining module.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `expSMulHom` publishes the body, and `coe_expSMulHom` (line 131) is proved `:= rfl`, so downstream unification can unfold the definition. No consumer needs to unfold it: the only use, `coe_expSMulHom_mem_map_kostantForm`, goes through `rw [coe_expSMulHom]`.

findings.evidence: `Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/NatInt.lean:173, `@[norm_cast]`) applies since `A` is `Ring` + `Module ℚ A`; `Int.cast_neg` is `@[simp]` (Mathlib/Data/Int/Cast/Basic.lean:83). The module docstrings themselves write `exp (t • x)` (Exp.lean:20) and `exp (t • ρ (eᵢ))` (Exponential.lean:111), not the spelling actually proved.
findings.fix: State all of these with the canonical `ℤ`-action: `exp (t • x)`, `exp (-(t • x))` (or `exp ((-t) • x)`, normalized by `neg_zsmul`), and `∑ i ∈ range k, t ^ i • Associative.dividedPower i x`; derive from `Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul` once inside the proofs. Same for `coe_expSMulHom` and all four Kostant-form lemmas.
findings.issue: The `zsmul` lemmas state a ℚ-scalar action on an integer cast, `exp ((t : ℚ) • x)`, while their right sides use genuine `zsmul` (`t ^ i • dividedPower i x`). Worse, the conjugation lemmas spell the second factor `exp (((-t : ℤ) : ℚ) • x)`, which is not simp-normal (`Int.cast_neg` is `@[simp]`, rewriting it to `-↑t • x`) and does not match the `exp a * b * exp (-a)` shape produced by `exp_ad_apply`/`exp_mulLeft_sub_mulRight_apply` in the same file, so the two halves of the API do not compose. Instances: Exp.lean:90, 98, 131, 136-138; Exponential.lean:72-79, 83-91 (line 88), 96-103, 116-121.

findings.evidence: Exp.lean:112-133 defines the `inv` field as `exp (-(... • x))` but only `coe_expSMulHom` is stated; Exponential.lean:109-115 argues about the inverse in prose with no lemma to cite. The repo does supply such lemmas elsewhere, e.g. `charOfPoint_apply_inv_coe` in TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/Basic.lean:106.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem coe_inv_expSMulHom {x : A} (hx : IsNilpotent x) (t : Multiplicative ℤ) : (((expSMulHom hx t)⁻¹ : Aˣ) : A) = exp (-((Multiplicative.toAdd t : ℤ) • x))`, provable from `map_inv` and `coe_expSMulHom` (or `(rfl)` on the `inv` field).
findings.issue: `expSMulHom` is `Units`-valued but only the `val` field has a characteristic lemma. There is no lemma computing `((expSMulHom hx t)⁻¹ : A)`, so `simp` gets stuck on any goal mentioning the inverse of a root subgroup element — precisely the fact the file's prose relies on (`exp_zsmul_apply_mem` docstring: "the inverse of `exp (t • ρ (eᵢ))` is `exp (-t • ρ (eᵢ))`") and the fact behind `exp_zsmul_conj_mem`.

summary: The `expSMulHom` body is exposed with no consumer that needs to unfold it, and its `rfl` coercion lemma leaks defeq; the unit's inverse has no characteristic lemma. Separately, every `*_zsmul_*` statement mixes a ℚ-cast smul on the left with genuine `zsmul` on the right and uses the non-simp-normal `((-t : ℤ) : ℚ)` spelling, so the lemmas do not match goals a consumer will actually have.
